characterization_methods.key_findings: S1100 yield strength 827 MPa and ultimate tensile strength 998 MPa, both lower than the other conditions; the engineering stress–strain curve peaks just below 1000 MPa but extends to ~60% strain
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature (25 °C), constant rate 3 mm/min, specimens machined along the rolling direction with gauge length 25 mm, gauge width 4 mm, gauge thickness 5 mm; yield strength determined as 0.2% offset strength; averages of three tests
characterization_methods.purpose: measure the tensile properties (yield strength and ultimate tensile strength) of the S1100 condition for comparison with S1000, S1050 and MHT

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Upstream ingot-preparation step shared by all heat-treatment conditions of this alloy.
For comparison of tensile properties only.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: measured values are averages of three tests per condition
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: gauge length 25 mm, gauge width 4 mm, gauge thickness 5 mm, along rolling direction

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Fig. 4(a) engineering stress–strain curve of S1100 (cyan): peaks just below the 1000 MPa gridline and extends furthest, to ~60% strain; Fig. 4(b) gives the corresponding true stress–strain and strain-hardening-rate curves; three strain-hardening stages I, II, III with a rate maximum of ~2000 MPa near strain 0.20–0.22

aliases: samples quenched after holding at 1100 °C for 3 min

unmapped_findings: S1100 was produced 'For comparison of tensile properties only' — it was not subjected to the full microstructural characterization (SEM/EBSD/TEM) or the Charpy impact testing performed on S1000, S1050 and MHT, so no grain size, grain-boundary fraction, precipitate or impact-energy data are reported for this sample.

From Fig. 4(a) the S1100 (cyan) engineering stress–strain curve peaks just below the 1000 MPa gridline and extends furthest, to about 60% strain; however no numeric total-elongation value for S1100 is given in the text or in Table 1 (which reports only S1000, S1050 and MHT).
